To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) Th17 cells require TGF beta for the sustained production of IL 17A and IL 17F, (2) in the absence of TFG beta, IL 12 and IL 23 act to suppress IL 23 and induce IFN gamma in a STAT4- and T bet-dependent fashion, (3) IL 12 is a potent inhibitor of the Th17 lineage and induces IFN gamma producing cells that are distinct from the Th17 lineage.

Th17 cell responses require TGF beta for their development, that Th17 cells are plastic and can differentiate into IFN gamma producing cells, and that the development of IFN gamma production is dependent on STAT4 and Tbet, and is regulated by IL12 and IL23.
Th17 cells are developmentally plastic, that Th17 cell plasticity is mediated by TGF beta, IL 12 and IL 23, and that the plasticity of Th17 cells can be exploited therapeutically.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and function of Th17 and Th1 cells.
the role of TGF beta and IL 23 in the development and function of IL 17 producing T cells.
the role of the immune system in the control of infection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Th17 cells are plastic, and can be induced to produce IFN-gamma, which is a key cytokine in host defense.
the Th17 cell lineage is not as fixed as once thought and is subject to late stage plasticity in the absence of Treg cells and TGF-beta.
Th17 cells are a distinct lineage with plasticity for IFN-gamma production.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Th17 lineage can be induced to become a Th1 lineage in the context of IL-12 and STAT4 signaling.
Th17 cells are not terminally committed to a single lineage, but can acquire a Th1 phenotype in the presence of IL-23 and IFN gamma, or IL-12 and IFN gamma.
Th1/Th17 plasticity exists and that it can be induced by IL-23 and IL-12.
The main takeaway from our work is that
TGFbeta is a critical factor for the development of Th17 cells.
Th17 cells can become Th1 cells.
Th17 cells have the potential to become Th1 cells, and that Th17 cells are not necessarily pathogenic.
